messages:
Avery: Quick sync — we need to standardize how we integrate OpenTelemetry across our inference services (python/go/rust). Key goals: low overhead, consistent resource/span naming, safe attrs (no PII), and a plan for exporting (OTLP -> collector vs direct exporters). Fast opinions?

Sam: +1. My vote: push metrics and traces through a local otel-collector sidecar (gRPC) to offload batching/sampling. Reduces SDK CPU spikes.

Priya: Sidecar makes sense for CPU-bound Rust/Go workers. For python (gunicorn/uvicorn) we need care around fork/shutdown — OTEL SDKs sometimes leak background threads. Important: init exporter after worker fork or use pre-fork hooks.

Jules: Right, python note: for gunicorn pre_fork/post_fork hooks are needed. Also set OTEL_PYTHON_CONTEXT to "async" for uvicorn to avoid contextvars issues with asyncio.

Marta: We should also standardize resource attributes: "service.name=redwood-inference", add model.name, model.version, deployment.env, region. Keep request_id and trace_id. Avoid high-cardinality user ids or prompt text.

Avery: Agreed on resource attrs. For span names propose: inference.request -> child spans: tokenize, model.forward, kv_cache_lookup, compile_kernels. Use attributes like token_count:int, kv_cache_hit:bool, batch_size:int. Thoughts on cardinality?

Sam: token_count/batch_size ok. kv_cache_hit boolean ok. But avoid storing prompt hashes in attr unless we salt and trim. Use hashed_prompt_id if needed for evals.

Priya: Sampling: default to parent-based with probabilistic sampling at 1% globally, then increase to 10% for errors and internal eval routes. We can also use tail-based sampling later in otel-collector for quality signals.

Jules: OTLP exporter config: use gRPC/4317 from SDKs to local collector. For direct-to-backend we lose batching and flexibility. Collector can do attribute filtering (PII redaction) & enrichments (add customer id mapping).

Marta: Retention question from Console: how long to keep traces in backend for debug vs cost. Propose 7 days for full traces, 30 days aggregated metrics. Long-term archive for sampled golden traces (manual retention tag).

Avery: Good. Also implement an exporter flush on SIGTERM, SIGINT for all languages. In Go use otel/sdk/resource and Shutdown(ctx) on server stop. Python use force_flush + shutdown in Gunicorn pre-stop. Rust: call tracer_provider.shutdown.

Sam: Practical perf knobs: batching_size=512, batch_timeout_ms=200, max_export_batch_size lower on memory-constrained machines. For Python set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_PROTOCOL to "grpc".

Priya: Instrumentation libs: opentelemetry-instrumentation for python, otelhttp/otellib for go, opentelemetry for rust. But avoid auto-instrumentation for model libs — prefer manual spans around forward passes to keep span semantics stable.

Jules: We should add one span event per token stream chunk for streaming endpoints (to analyze tail latency). But sample those heavily to avoid explosion.

Marta: Security: ensure exporter endpoints authenticate (mTLS or API key). Collector should be the only component allowed to reach telemetry backend. Logs must carry traceparent header to correlate.

Avery: Implementation plan idea: phase 1 (staging): sidecar collector + SDK init + resource attrs + basic spans + flush on shutdown. Phase 2 (canary): add streaming events, tail-based sampling, and PII redaction filters. Phase 3 (GA): metrics + dashboards + retention policy.

Priya: Tests: add e2e that starts process, runs a request, asserts that a span with name "inference.request" and attributes model.name/model.version exist in OTLP payload (we can capture via test-collector). Also add unit test for shutdown flush.

Sam: Ops: add config via env var precedence doc (service-specific env > docker image env > deploy defaults). Document differences across SDKs (python env var names vs go).

Jules: One more gotcha: in Python, multiprocess workers sometimes share SDK state if you init early. Recommend lazy init inside request-handling process or use pre/post fork properly.

Marta: Any opinions on keeping traces vs using only metrics for high-volume routes?

Avery: For heavy paths (e.g., batch infer with thousands qps) prefer aggregated metrics + sparse traces. We can tag some requests with debug:true to force full trace export.

Sam: +1. Also queue telemetry to local tmp file on export failures (disk-backed batching) for short outages. Collector handles retries but SDK-level buffering helps.

Priya: Implementation note for Rust: tokio runtime + otel exporter must be spawned on same runtime, use tracing-opentelemetry or instrument with tracing crate then bridge to otel.

Jules: Ok next steps: @Sam please draft collector config for sidecar (sampling, tail-sampling, attribute processors). @Priya draft per-language init patterns + SIGTERM flush examples. I'll compile docs and a rollout checklist.

Sam: On it. I'll push a staging config and share link: <https://git.redwood/infra/otel-collector/staging-config> :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: otel-collector config v0.9 deployed to staging-cluster-alpha at 2024-05-07T18:22:10Z

Marta: Thanks — can we add a field in Console to toggle telemetry debug traces per-deployment? Would help debugging without global sampling changes.

Avery: Yes, add a per-deployment telemetry toggle (boolean) and a note that enabling will increase export volume. We'll wire that into rollout checklist.

Sam: I'll also add a short example env snippet in the doc: `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:4317 OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=parentbased_traceidratio OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG=0.01`

Priya: Love it. Let's meet tomorrow 10am to review collector config & docs.

Avery: Thanks all, will create the doc and link in #eng-platform when ready. :rocket:
